ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: To visit and consult a true teacher is the itinerant act of going to someone able to expose and settle the matter in direct encounter.
EvidenceBody: The Bloodstream Treatise says that one who has not clarified must consult such a person to settle the root of birth and death, while denying the title to anyone who has not seen directly. A lamp address describes itinerants arriving at a community, setting down bowl and flask, and then meeting that person.

Later masters include consultation among leaving home, traveling on foot, entering retreat, and raising a saying, but also ask listeners to identify the single present action running through all of them.

DraftEvidence.ZenBend: Travel to a knowledgeable person becomes a defining Chan itinerary whose target must itself pass the corpus's test for a true teacher.
DraftEvidence.CounterexampleOrLimit: The honorific is not automatic: an exact source explicitly says someone without direct sight is not a true teacher.

ComparedThings: to visit and consult a true teacher
its attested grammatical and rhetorical deployments
DifferentThingTest.Reason: Travel, arrival, and enumeration all name consulting a qualifying teacher; different journey stages do not split the act.

DraftEvidence.AliasRationale: Visit, consult, call on, teacher, master, and good-knowing friend support English retrieval.

ModifierControls.Finding: The Bloodstream Treatise supplies an explicit eligibility test for the consulted person.

FamilyControls.Finding: The extended Sudhana formula is a separate narrative sequence, not every Chan consultation.
